question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (AMD)

calls.reasoning: Non-GAAP consensus ~$1.94 (rev ~$13.06B, guided $13B±0.3B); AMD beat by 4-5c last two quarters -> non-GAAP ~$2.00. Recurring GAAP gap ex-investment items ~$0.55 (SBC ~0.30, intangibles amortization ~0.33, acq costs ~0.02, offset by ~+0.10 tax), consistent with Q1'26 gap 0.53 and Q2'26 ex-gain gap ~0.57 -> GAAP ~$1.45. Hudson Labs lists GAAP consensus ~$1.42. Main swing: Q2 had a $483M (+$0.29) gain on newly public equity stakes; $1.1B+ restricted listed holdings get marked each quarter -> ±~$0.15. Market check: only Polymarket 'AMD beat (non-GAAP) EPS' Yes 0.88, ~$635 volume; wrong metric (non-GAAP beat), not an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off GAAP diluted EPS in AMD's Q3 FY2026 earnings release (scheduled Nov 3, 2026 after close), not non-GAAP EPS. Event window: first release after Sep 30, 2026 -> report expected Nov 3, 2026; as of 2026-10-29 the report is not yet out (quarter ended ~Sep 26, 2026).
- Q2 2026 (AMD PR/8-K, Aug 4 2026): revenue $11.5B, GAAP diluted EPS $1.38, non-GAAP $1.66, GAAP net income $2,297M, diluted shares 1,659M.
- Q2 2026 reconciliation items per share: SBC +0.30 ($503M), amortization of acquisition intangibles +0.33 ($544M), gains on long-term investments -0.29 (-$483M), acquisition-related costs +0.02, legal loss contingency +0.01, income tax provision -0.10 (-$161M).
- Q1 2026: GAAP EPS $0.84 vs non-GAAP $1.37 (gap 0.53). Q2 2025: GAAP $0.54 vs non-GAAP $0.48. From memory (not verified this run): Q3'25 GAAP 0.75 vs non-GAAP 1.20; Q4'25 GAAP ~0.92 vs non-GAAP ~1.53.
- Q2 10-Q (sec.gov): $483M net gain on long-term investments came from equity stakes that became publicly traded in Q2 2026 (reclassified to Level 1); long-term investments include $1.1B fair value of marketable equity subject to sale restrictions through Oct 2028 -> marked to market each quarter, either direction.
- Q3 2026 guidance (Aug 4): revenue ~$13B ± $0.3B, non-GAAP gross margin ~56%.
- Consensus (MarketBeat/others, late Oct 2026): non-GAAP EPS ~$1.93-1.94, revenue ~$13.0-13.06B. AMD beat non-GAAP consensus in Q2 ($1.66 vs ~$1.61-1.62).
- Hudson Labs preview lists a 'GAAP' consensus EPS of $1.42 (its other numbers look internally inconsistent; treat with caution). A Barchart/Webull preview mentions $1.67 expected 'diluted' EPS (unclear basis).
- Status quo: GAAP = non-GAAP minus a recurring ~$0.53-0.60 gap (SBC + amortization - tax effect), plus or minus investment marks and one-offs.
- Searched but not found: which companies AMD's newly public equity stakes are, and how those stocks moved in Q3 2026; any announced Q3 restructuring/impairment; how OpenAI warrant tranches hit GAAP results.
calls.reference_class: AMD recent quarters' GAAP-vs-non-GAAP EPS gap (Q3'25 0.45, Q4'25 ~0.61, Q1'26 0.53, Q2'26 0.28 incl. investment gain) applied to non-GAAP consensus plus typical beat

calls.reasoning: Non-GAAP consensus ~$1.94 (rev ~$13.06B vs $13B±0.3B guide); AMD typically beats by ~4-5c -> ~$1.98. Recurring GAAP gap (SBC ~0.30 + intangibles ~0.33 + acq costs, less tax) ~$0.53-0.57 -> GAAP ~$1.43, consistent with a cited GAAP consensus of $1.42. Volatile marks on ~$1.1B of restricted listed equity (Q2 had +$0.29) give two-sided risk; OpenAI/Meta warrant contra-revenue if a tranche vests with MI450 shipments skews the downside. Polymarket non-GAAP 'beat' contract (0.88, ~$635 vol) is a different metric and not used as an anchor.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agreed on the facts: Q2'26 GAAP 1.38 / non-GAAP 1.66, Q1'26 0.84 / 1.37, recurring gap ~0.53-0.57, non-GAAP consensus ~1.94, cited GAAP consensus 1.42, and the warrants accounted as contra-revenue with nothing vested through Q2. The disagreements were judgment calls about tail width (Run 2 was widest because it weighted the ±0.3 investment swing and warrant risk more heavily). Two factual unknowns can't be settled offline: which equity stakes produced the Q2 gain and how they moved in Q3, and whether any warrant tranche vested in Q3. I kept the shared central estimate (~1.43), used a downside tail slightly wider than Runs 1 and 3 for the warrant and impairment risk, and carried forward a small p_below_lower for a large one-off charge.
